good: Speed, boost and takedown HUD react.
Trailer shows a rival and two takedown awards.
bad: Car stays stuck against walls despite steering and boost.
Box cars and an empty, flat world look crude.
Particles obscure collisions; wall slams and rival wrecks are unclear.
gpt-6.1-sol-high.one_line: The boost and takedown text promise action, but most of the drive is spent stuck against a wall.

good: Winding elevated highway with glowing lamps, barriers and a sunset palette — real bends to carve
HUD is properly Burnout: big MPH readout, boost bar, takedown counter, rival distance
Takedowns actually register with a big TAKEDOWN!/BOOST TAKEDOWN! banner and a counting rival
bad: The filmed drive crawls at 1-3 mph — the car stalls and barely moves for most of the test
Reverse failed and steering only creeps the car sideways at walking pace
Trailer shows 236 mph speed and takedowns the scripted drive never reproduces
step-5-preview.one_line: Great bones — sunset highway, real bends, punchy takedown HUD — but the car crawls at 3 mph in the actual drive, so the Burnout fantasy only lives in the trailer.

good: Winding road with barriers, lamp posts and a strong sunset palette
Trailer shows a big TAKEDOWN! banner, a takedown counter, a rival distance tag and a 248 mph boost
Burnout-like HUD: big italic speed number and a glowing boost bar
bad: In the filmed drive the car hits the wall and stays stuck at 1-3 mph under a cloud of smoke for about 50 s, with no crash and no respawn
Steering and reverse cannot be checked because the car is stuck; the 102 mph in the S phase looks like a reset, not reverse
The cars are blocky boxes, and the rival is never close in live play
opus-5.5-high.one_line: The trailer sells a neon takedown racer, but when I actually played it, I spent the whole run grinding against the first wall at 2 mph.

good: Winding road with barriers, street lamps and a red sunset
The trailer shows 'TAKEDOWN!' text, a 'BOOST TAKEDOWN!' popup and the takedown counter going up
The HUD has big italic MPH, a blue boost bar, a takedown counter and the distance to the rival
bad: In the scripted drive, the car hits the wall at 5 s and stays stuck at 1-3 mph behind smoke for about 60 s, with no 'crashed' message and no respawn
Steering, drift and boost do not visibly work in the test film, and reverse cannot be read
The cars are rough box models, and the smoke particles cover the screen
opus-5.5.one_line: The trailer looks like a real Burnout duel, but when I drove it myself I got stuck on the first wall and sat in smoke for a whole minute.

good: Chase cam holds the car and the road genuinely bends, so forward speed reads fast (127-248 mph)
Takedown is called out with a big TAKEDOWN!/BOOST TAKEDOWN banner and the counter ticks 1 to 2
HUD has the Burnout staples: giant speed, segmented boost bar, takedown count, rival gap
bad: Huge white bokeh particle cloud floods the screen after any gas/boost and never clears, hiding the car and road
After the crash the speed sits at 1-2 mph for 30+ seconds with no fast respawn, so steering and reverse never register
World is a flat dark plane under a red gradient with boxy cars and featureless sky; the rival wreck itself is never visible
deepseek-v4.1-flash.one_line: It looks the Burnout part with a big speedo and a TAKEDOWN banner, but the screen turns into a snowstorm of particles and then the car just dies stuck at 1 mph.
